## Adding more sample metadata

```{r}
scz_spatial@sample_meta <- scz_spatial@sample_meta %>% left_join(samples_metadata, by = c("sample_name" = "DxID"))
```

## Filtering

### Using Control Probes and Codewords

First we create a function that we can use with lapply that takes the filtering thresholds that we found previously as well as the counts matrix as inputs. Notice that the thresholds are named arguments meaning they have default values set to the exact variables we were working with earlier. We find the combined expression within each cell of each of the three associated controls using column sums and identify the cell IDs where the combined expression of any one of these types of controls is greater than or equal to the 99th percentile threshold. Finally, we take a union of the identified cell IDs.

By calling this function with `lapply`, we'll have named list (`to_remove_all`) where the sample name stores a vector of cell IDs that should be removed for that sample.

We use a `for` loop to then loop through the sample names and actually filter the cell IDs within the count matrix. Recall that the cells correspond to the columns in the count matrix. Our filter is specifically using an exclamation point (`!`) to specify that if a column name is **not** the list of cell IDs to be filtered, then keep it.

```{r}
findOverlap <- function(mat, negcp = negcontrol_probe_cutoff, negcc = negcontrol_cdwd_cutoff, ucc = unassigned_cdwd_cutoff){
    which_negcp <- names(which(mat[startsWith(rownames(mat), "NegControlProbe"), ] %>% Matrix::colSums() >= negcp))
    which_negcc <- names(which(mat[startsWith(rownames(mat), "NegControlCodeword"), ] %>% Matrix::colSums() >= negcc))
    which_ucc <- names(which(mat[startsWith(rownames(mat), "Unassigned"), ] %>% Matrix::colSums() >= ucc))

    to_remove <- union(union(which_negcp, which_negcc), which_ucc)

    return(to_remove)
}

to_remove_all <- lapply(scz_spatial@counts function(x) findOverlap(x))

for (sample_name in names(to_remove_all)){
    scz_spatial@counts[[sample_name]] <- scz_spatial@counts[[sample_name]][,!colnames(scz_spatial@counts[[sample_name]]) %in% to_remove_all[[sample_name]]]
}
```

How many cells do we have per sample now?

```{r}
lapply(scz_spatial@counts, function(i) ncol(i))
```

We also want to remove the spatial metadata information about these cells since they're no longer in the counts matrix. Recall that each row corresponds to a cell, and the cell IDs are stored in the `libname` column of the `spatial_meta` slot.

```{r}
for (sample_name in names(to_remove_all)){
    scz_spatial@spatial_meta[[sample_name]] <- scz_spatial@spatial_meta[[sample_name]][!scz_spatial@spatial_meta[[sample_name]]$libname %in% to_remove_all[[sample_name]],]
}
```

### Removing Control Probes and Codewords

Now that we've used the control probes and codewords to filter out cells, we can remove them as "genes" from our counts matrix.

```{r}
for (sample_name in names(scz_spatial@counts)){
    scz_spatial@counts[[sample_name]] <- scz_spatial@counts[[sample_name]][!grepl("^NegControl|Unassigned",rownames(scz_spatial@counts[[sample_name]])), ]
}
```

All of the counts matrices will now be 300 rows representing data for the 300 Xenium panel genes.

```{r}
lapply(scz_spatial@counts, function(i) nrow(i))
```

### Using spatialGE

The filtering that we've done, while important, isn't enough. We also need to consider the overall library size of and number of features in cells. 

<!--
Fill in explanation of why
-->

```{r}
scz_spatial <- spatialGE::filter_data(scz_spatial,
                           spot_minreads=50,
                           spot_maxreads=3500,
                           spot_mingenes=10)
```

What do the summary statistics and distributions look like now?

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Table

```{r}
summarize_STlist(scz_spatial) %>% print(width = Inf)
```

Notice that the number of cells retained decreased for each sample again. Some decreased by only about one hundred while another sample decreased by a little over two thousand!

## Normalizing

Transformation with `spatialGE` uses either log-transformation or the `SCTransform` method. 

We'll need a second `STlist` object so we can run two different transformations and compare them.

```{r}
scz_spatial_tr <- rlang::duplicate(scz_spatial)
```

### Log Transformation

Explain log transformation.

```{r}
scz_spatial <- spatialGE::transform_data(scz_spatial, method='log', cores=2)
```

### SCTransform

Explain SCTransform method.

```{r}
scz_spatial_tr <- transform_data(scz_spatial_tr, method = 'sct', cores = 2)
```

### Visualize

We can visualize the library size for each cell within each sample.

```{r}
visualize_lib_size <- function(mat, title_name){
    Matrix::colSums(mat) %>% 
        as.data.frame() %>%
        ggplot(aes(x=`.`)) + geom_histogram(bins = 500) + theme_bw() + ggtitle(title_name)
}

patchwork::wrap_plots(purrr::map2(scz_spatial@counts, names(scz_spatial@counts), visualize_lib_size), nrow = 2) + patchwork::plot_annotation(title = "Raw counts")

wrap_plots(purrr::map2(scz_spatial@tr_counts, names(scz_spatial@tr_counts), visualize_lib_size), nrow = 2) + plot_annotation(title = "Log transformed counts")

wrap_plots(map2(scz_spatial_tr@tr_counts, names(scz_spatial_tr@tr_counts), visualize_lib_size), nrow = 2) + plot_annotation(title = "SCTransform counts")

```

We can visualize the distribution of expression of a few genes (before and after the normalization) using the `distribution_plots()` function.

```{r}
raw_plots <- distribution_plots(scz_spatial, genes = c("CX3CR1", "FKBP5", "PVALB", "MBP"), data_type = "raw")

transformed_log_plots <- distribution_plots(scz_spatial, genes = c("CX3CR1", "FKBP5", "PVALB", "MBP"), data_type = "tr")

transformed_sct_plots <- distribution_plots(scz_spatial_tr, genes = c("CX3CR1", "FKBP5", "PVALB", "MBP"), data_type = "tr")
```

:::{.panel-tabset}

#### CX3CR1

```{r}
raw_plots$CX3CR1 + transformed_log_plots$CX3CR1 + transformed_sct_plots$CX3CR1 + patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect", nrow=3)
```

#### FKBP5

```{r}
raw_plots$FKBP5 + transformed_log_plots$FKBP5 + transformed_sct_plots$FKBP5 + patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect", nrow=3)
```

#### PVALB

```{r}
raw_plots$PVALB + transformed_log_plots$PVALB + transformed_sct_plots$PVALB + patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect", nrow=3)
```

#### MBP

```{r}
raw_plots$MBP + transformed_log_plots$MBP + transformed_sct_plots$MBP + patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect", nrow=3)
```

:::

Now we want to clear up some R memory

```{r}
rm(raw_plots, transformed_log_plots, transformed_sct_plots)
gc()
```

saveRDS(scz_spatial, here("data/wrangled/scz_spatial.rds"))
